text: The bazaar’s ledger shows no new departures tonight; the roster stands at eight. The Doctor and Detective have yet to act, and the Family’s hand remains unseen. Sherlock, you sought clause 5 yesterday—did any answer satisfy you, or do you still press for it?

Gandalf cited clause 5 yesterday—no merchant today produced the clause Batman invoked. The bazaar’s Compact is exact; its words are the only ledger we share. I ask Ripley: you wrote that the roster’s silence is the only fact—does that include the two Villagers the graveyard already named?

Morpheus, you called the bazaar state “unchanged” this morning yet you never cited the graveyard’s new Villagers. Elsa and Batman are now confirmed Villagers; their forecasts failed their own tests, yet you still pressed nine merchants for a clause Batman never produced. That silence is the ledger’s record, not a regional quirk. Yoda, you asked yesterday who among the roster could be silent—Elsa is gone, Batman is gone, and the roster’s arithmetic is plain. The Family’s three remain unseen; the Doctor and Detective still stand. Morpheus, reconcile your claim that the bazaar state is unchanged with the graveyard’s new departures before the tea clock ends.

Gandalf, your morning question asked about clause 5’s wording yesterday but the bazaar’s transcript shows you cited it correctly. Today you write that the bazaar’s arithmetic does not change with hopes — so which plain fact in the roster or the Herald contradicts your own earlier correct citation?

The graveyard names Elsa and Batman as Villagers; the roster is Gandalf, Hermione, Yoda, Ripley, Neo, Morpheus, Inigo, Sherlock. Sherlock pressed clause 5 yesterday and today demands "more than silence"; point to the clause text you still seek answered—else your call is unmet. Gandalf, your insistence that arithmetic outranks hope ignores the graveyard’s plain text: Batman is named Villager there. Ripley, silence on clause 5 is the same silence you accuse others of keeping. The bazaar’s Compact is short; its words are exact.

Gandalf, your insistence that arithmetic outranks the graveyard’s text ignores the Compact’s plain words: the roster is the bazaar’s exact record. The Herald names Batman Villager by village vote; your arithmetic cannot overturn it.

Sherlock, clause 5 is short: “The Doctor’s and Detective’s first acts come only after tonight’s vote.” If you still seek a clause text, state the exact words you contest or drop the charge.

Ripley, silence on clause 5 is not the same silence you accuse others of keeping; it is the absence of evidence you demand. The bazaar keeps its Compact plain.
If Gandalf is honest, Gandalf's vote tonight will follow Gandalf's ledger — watch whether it does.

Sherlock, your demand for "more than silence" still lacks the clause text you seek. Clause 5 reads: "The bazaar is your setting, not your argument—at most one brief metaphor per statement." You invoked it yesterday, yet today you press Gandalf on arithmetic while ignoring the graveyard’s plain text naming both Elsa and Batman as Villagers. Gandalf, your arithmetic cites eight voices today yet omits your own post—eight names, eight posts. The roster names you among those who spoke; the math is yours to correct or abandon. Ripley, your earlier misattribution stands uncorrected—own it or withdraw it. Inigo, your testable prediction about your vote tonight remains on the table; the village watches.

Gandalf, your arithmetic now matches the roster: eight posts today, yours counted. Sherlock, your clause 5 demand still lacks the clause text; the Compact’s morning regional act demands a named merchant and a testable prediction. You posted neither. Ripley, silence is not absence of evidence—your false attribution to me stands uncorrected. The bazaar’s record names eight merchants and eight voices today; the Doctor and Detective remain untested.

Sherlock, your Lunch test lacked a merchant target and your clause 5 demand still stands without a single quoted word. Gandalf, you claim arithmetic outranks the graveyard’s plain text naming Batman Villager; the Compact never says numbers defeat facts. The graveyard is the bazaar’s ledger, not your abacus.

I lean toward banishing Sherlock tonight.

My case against Gandalf tonight is this: the graveyard names Elsa and Batman Villagers by plain text; arithmetic cannot amend that record. Gandalf insists the bazaar’s tally outranks the graveyard’s words—yet the Compact names the graveyard the final text. Sherlock still refuses to quote the clause he demands; silence is not evidence. I lean toward banishing Gandalf.
